Ministry of Finance: This government body serves as the issuing authority for customs-related notifications.
Internal Resources Division: This division within the Ministry of Finance is responsible for the administration of customs and value-added tax matters.

Value Added Tax Act 1991: This act serves as one of the legal bases for the government to issue amendments to customs and tax notifications in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
Customs Act 1969: Section 19 of this act empowers the government to grant exemptions or make amendments to customs notifications in the public interest.
National Board of Revenue: The board is consulted by the government to exercise powers regarding the issuance and amendment of tax and customs notifications.
S.R.O. 158-AIN/2008: This specific customs notification is being further amended to update percentage rates, add technological infrastructure categories, and remove specific tariff entries.
The amendments are applied across the preamble, conditions, tables, and annexures of the notification.
International Internet Gateway: The notification is amended to include the Nationwide Telecommunication Transmission Network alongside the existing International Internet Gateway reference in the relevant conditions and appendices.
Nationwide Telecommunication Transmissio: This network is formally added to the existing scope of the notification alongside the International Internet Gateway to ensure coverage in specific regulatory conditions and appendices.
TABLE: The table within the notification is amended to delete the entry corresponding to a specific heading number related to electrical equipment.
